history.summary: CSV IDENTITY FLAG: 'Sai Mandir' is a generic name - the documented referent in Soreng district is the Sri Sathya Sai Sarva Dharma Kendra at Daramdin village (near Soreng town). CSV town 'Soreng' is district-correct; the actual village is Daramdin. NOT AN OLD HINDU TEMPLE: it is a modern interfaith (Sarva Dharma) centre of the Sathya Sai Baba movement - Wikipedia explicitly notes it is often mislabeled a Hindu temple. The foundation stone was laid in December 2002 by CM Pawan Kumar Chamling; land was donated by local families (Rizal, Pradhan) and it was inaugurated on 15 April 2007 (flag: one travel page says 'foundation stone December 2012' while giving inauguration 2007 - internally inconsistent; the 2002 foundation date rests on the better-sourced account, verify). K.N. Rizal has been caretaker since 2007. Annual events are held here by different religious groups. Nearby: the 'Swarga Jane Sidi' (Stairway to Heaven) monument/folklore site (construction resumed after a halt - verify) and the Batasey Dara viewpoint over the Singhalila range.

name: Sri Sathya Sai Sarva Dharma Kendra (Sai Mandir)
town: Daramdin village, Soreng district (CSV town 'Soreng' is district-correct; actual village Daramdin)
town_description: Daramdin is a village near Soreng town in Soreng district, West Sikkim, unusual for its broad flat terrain ('Dalom' - a place of rest, in Lepcha). The Sai centre stands at its centre; the village also has a government secondary school, a university campus, and folklore about an ancient tower of clay vessels built toward the sky.
tradition: Sathya Sai Baba movement - interfaith Sarva Dharma centre (NOT a Hindu temple; not a Buddhist monastery)

travel.road: About 120 km from Gangtok by road; accessible via Soreng town by taxi/shared vehicle (verify).
